plan.topic_summary: Chiplet architectures decompose monolithic SoCs into multiple smaller dies connected through advanced packaging, reshaping semiconductor design, manufacturing, and the competitive balance between foundries, OSATs, and fabless designers. Over a 1–5 year horizon, the pace of adoption, standardization progress, and packaging cost curves will determine whether chiplets become the dominant design paradigm or remain confined to a subset of high-end applications.
key_questions: What is the current adoption rate of chiplet-based designs in high-performance computing and data center accelerators, and which packaging technologies are reaching volume production?
What are the primary yield, cost, and thermal bottlenecks limiting chiplet adoption at leading-edge process nodes today?
How is the die-to-die interconnect standardization landscape evolving, and what impact will it have on the competitive dynamics between foundries and OSATs over the next 1–3 years?
What are the thermal and power density limits of current 2.5D and 3D packaging approaches, and what next-generation solutions are being pursued?
Will chiplet architectures deliver meaningful total cost of ownership reduction at advanced nodes over a 3–5 year horizon, or will packaging complexity and interconnect overhead offset the benefits?
How might widespread chiplet adoption reshape the value chain and revenue distribution among fabless designers, foundries, and packaging providers by 2028–2030?

sources.title: HexaMesh: Scaling to Hundreds of Chiplets with an Optimized Chiplet Arrangement
sources.abstract: 2.5D integration is an important technique to tackle the growing cost of manufacturing chips in advanced technology nodes. This poses the challenge of providing high-performance inter-chiplet interconnects (ICIs). As the number of chiplets grows to tens or hundreds, it becomes infeasible to hand-optimize their arrangement in a way that maximizes the ICI performance. In this paper, we propose HexaMesh, an arrangement of chiplets that outperforms a grid arrangement both in theory (network diameter reduced by 42%; bisection bandwidth improved by 130%) and in practice (latency reduced by 19%; throughput improved by 34%). MexaMesh enables large-scale chiplet designs with high-performance ICIs.

sources.title: MFIT: Multi-Fidelity Thermal Modeling for 2.5D and 3D Multi-Chiplet Architectures
sources.abstract: Rapidly evolving artificial intelligence and machine learning applications require ever-increasing computational capabilities, while monolithic 2D design technologies approach their limits. Heterogeneous integration of smaller chiplets using a 2.5D silicon interposer and 3D packaging has emerged as a promising paradigm to address this limit and meet performance demands. These approaches offer a significant cost reduction and higher manufacturing yield than monolithic 2D integrated circuits. However, the compact arrangement and high compute density exacerbate the thermal management challenges, potentially compromising performance. Addressing these thermal modeling challenges is critical, especially as system sizes grow and different design stages require varying levels of accuracy and speed. Since no single thermal modeling technique meets all these needs, this paper introduces MFIT, a range of multi-fidelity thermal models that effectively balance accuracy and speed. These multi-fidelity models can enable efficient design space exploration and runtime thermal management. Our extensive testing on systems with 16, 36, and 64 2.5D integrated chiplets and 16x3 3D integrated chiplets demonstrates that these models can reduce execution times from days to mere seconds and milliseconds with negligible loss in accuracy.

sources.title: Automated Design of Chiplets
sources.abstract: Chiplet-based designs have gained recognition as a promising alternative to monolithic SoCs due to their lower manufacturing costs, improved re-usability, and optimized technology specialization. Despite progress made in various related domains, the design of chiplets remains largely reliant on manual processes. sources.title: Chiplets on Wheels: Review Paper on Holistic Chiplet Solutions for Autonomous Vehicles
sources.abstract: On the advent of the slow death of Moore's law, the silicon industry is moving towards a new era of chiplets. The automotive industry is experiencing a profound transformation towards software-defined vehicles, fueled by the surging demand for automotive compute chips, expected to reach 20-22 billion by 2030. High-performance compute (HPC) chips become instrumental in meeting the soaring demand for computational power. Various strategies, including centralized electrical and electronic architecture and the innovative Chiplet Systems, are under exploration. The latter, breaking down System-on-Chips (SoCs) into functional units, offers unparalleled customization and integration possibilities. The research accentuates the crucial open Chiplet ecosystem, fostering collaboration and enhancing supply chain resilience. In this paper, we address the unique challenges that arise when attempting to leverage chiplet-based architecture to design a holistic silicon solution for the automotive industry. We propose a throughput-oriented micro-architecture for ADAS and infotainment systems alongside a novel methodology to evaluate chiplet architectures. Further, we develop in-house simulation tools leveraging the gem5 framework to simulate latency and throughput. Finally, we perform an extensive design of thermally-aware chiplet placement and develop a micro-fluids-based cooling design.

sources.title: Chiplet Design and Heterogeneous Integration Packaging
Floorplet: Performance-aware Floorplan Framework for Chiplet Integration
sources.abstract: A chiplet is an integrated circuit that encompasses a well-defined subset of an overall system's functionality. In contrast to traditional monolithic system-on-chips (SoCs), chiplet-based architecture can reduce costs and increase reusability, representing a promising avenue for continuing Moore's Law. Despite the advantages of multi-chiplet architectures, floorplan design in a chiplet-based architecture has received limited attention. Conflicts between cost and performance necessitate a trade-off in chiplet floorplan design since additional latency introduced by advanced packaging can decrease performance. Consequently, balancing power, performance, cost, area, and reliability is of paramount importance. To address this challenge, we propose Floorplet, a framework comprising simulation tools for performance reporting and comprehensive models for cost and reliability optimization. Our framework employs the open-source Gem5 simulator to establish the relationship between performance and floorplan for the first time, guiding the floorplan optimization of multi-chiplet architecture. The experimental results show that our framework decreases inter-chiplet communication costs by 24.81%.

sources.title: Chiplet-LEGO: Delivering Multiple Voltage Rails to Chiplets with Chiplet VRMs
sources.venue: IEEE ... Workshop on Control and Modeling for Power Electronics
sources.abstract: This paper presents Chiplet-LEGO, a single-input multiple-output (SIMO) linear extendable group operated (LEGO) voltage regulator module (VRM) architecture as a new development of the LEGO-VRM family. This architecture not only offers a high voltage conversion ratio but also delivers multiple individually regulated output voltages, making it well-suited for VRMs in system-on-chip (SoC) applications with multiple voltage rails. The Chiplet-LEGO is well suited to numerous numbers of independently regulated output voltages with scalable power capability. Dynamic models were derived to understand the cross-regulation behaviors. A 24 V-to-1 V 120 W dual-output Chiplet-LEGO prototype with discrete components was built and tested to evaluate the effectiveness of the analysis.

sources.title: The Survey of Chiplet-based Integrated Architecture: An EDA perspective
sources.abstract: Enhancing performance while reducing costs is the fundamental design philosophy of integrated circuits (ICs). With advancements in packaging technology, interposer-based chiplet architecture has emerged as a promising solution. Chiplet integration, often referred to as 2.5D IC, offers significant benefits, including cost-effectiveness, reusability, and improved performance. However, realizing these advantages heavily relies on effective electronic design automation (EDA) processes. EDA plays a crucial role in optimizing architecture design, partitioning, combination, physical design, reliability analysis, etc. Currently, optimizing the automation methodologies for chiplet architecture is a popular focus; therefore, we propose a survey to summarize current methods and discuss future directions. This paper will review the research literature on design automation methods for chiplet-based architectures, highlighting current challenges and exploring opportunities in 2.5D IC from an EDA perspective. We expect this survey will provide valuable insights for the future development of EDA tools for chiplet-based integrated architectures.

sources.title: Chiplet-Gym: Optimizing Chiplet-Based AI Accelerator Design With Reinforcement Learning
sources.abstract: Modern Artificial Intelligence (AI) workloads demand computing systems with large silicon area to sustain throughput and competitive performance. However, prohibitive manufacturing costs and yield limitations at advanced tech nodes and die-size reaching the reticle limit restrain us from achieving this. With the recent innovations in advanced packaging technologies, chiplet-based architectures have gained significant attention in the AI hardware domain. However, the vast design space of chiplet-based AI accelerator design and the absence of system and package-level co-design methodology make it difficult for the designer to find the optimum design point regarding Power, Performance, Area, and manufacturing Cost (PPAC). This paper presents Chiplet-Gym, a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based optimization framework to explore the vast design space of chiplet-based AI accelerators, encompassing the resource allocation, placement, and packaging architecture. We analytically model the PPAC of the chiplet-based AI accelerator and integrate it into an OpenAI gym environment to evaluate the design points. We also explore non-RL-based optimization approaches and combine these two approaches to ensure the robustness of the optimizer. The optimizer-suggested design point achieves$1.52\boldsymbol{\times}$throughput,$0.27\boldsymbol{\times}$energy, and$0.89\boldsymbol{\times}$cost of its monolithic counterpart at iso-area.

sources.title: Chiplet Placement Order Exploration Based on Learning to Rank with Graph Representation
sources.abstract: Chiplet-based systems, integrating various silicon dies manufactured at different integrated circuit technology nodes on a carrier interposer, have garnered significant attention in recent years due to their cost-effectiveness and competitive performance. The widespread adoption of reinforcement learning as a sequential placement method has introduced a new challenge in determining the optimal placement order for each chiplet. The order in which chiplets are placed on the interposer influences the spatial resources available for earlier and later placed chiplets, making the placement results highly sensitive to the sequence of chiplet placement. To address these challenges, we propose a learning to rank approach with graph representation, building upon the reinforcement learning framework RLPlanner. This method aims to select the optimal chiplet placement order for each chiplet-based system. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to placement order obtained solely based on the descending order of the chiplet area and the number of interconnect wires between the chiplets, utilizing the placement order obtained from the learning to rank network leads to further improvements in system temperature and inter-chiplet wirelength. Specifically, applying the top-ranked placement order obtained from the learning to rank network results in a 10.05% reduction in total inter-chiplet wirelength and a 1.01% improvement in peak system temperature during the chiplet placement process.

sources.title: Reliability and Chiplets
sources.abstract: Chiplet technology is a favored way to push Moore’s law to overcome the chip shrinkage problem, where the smaller scale needed leads to smaller yields. Through chiplets, smaller functional building blocks can be interconnected as needed in flexible ways and scale with new advantages. There are reliability challenges, but they can be overcome with good reliability engineering and practice. The resulting chiplet technology brings new advantages too. With these new advantages comes the potential for greater reliability for the customer. In this column, I explore chiplets, and I invite you to “chip in”!.

sources.title: Fengshui: Demystifying Chiplet Ecosystem and Bespoke Neural Network Accelerator Codesign
sources.abstract: Modern ML workloads, with stringent latency and energy constraints, are increasingly hard to run efficiently on homogeneous commodity hardware. We argue that operator-level disaggregation--tailoring microarchitecture, batching, and memory hierarchy to each operator--is essential to overcome these limitations, though the resulting highly bespoke accelerators incur prohibitive Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE) costs. Chiplet-based integration amortizes NRE across applications, but choosing which chiplets to build and how to compose them into accelerators is circularly dependent--a chiplet pool's value depends on the constructed accelerators, while accelerator quality is constrained by available chiplets. This paper introduces Fengshui, a chiplet ecosystem and accelerator co-design framework that jointly optimizes chiplet pool composition and bespoke application-specific integrated circuit (BASIC) design. Fengshui constructs BASICs through operator-level disaggregation, co-exploring chiplet and memory heterogeneity, tensor fusion, and pipeline/tensor/expert parallelism with place-and-route validation for physical implementability. With just 8 strategically selected chiplets, encompassing network switches, processing-in-memory units, and accelerators with diverse microarchitectures, Fengshui-generated BASICs achieve 48.5%, 88.1%, 93.0%, and 97.8% reductions in energy, energy-cost product (EC), energy-delay product (EDP), and energy-delay-cost product (EDPC) over homogeneous accelerators, while scoring within 4.1% of unconstrained heterogeneous designs across diverse neural networks. For datacenter MoE and dense LLM serving, Fengshui reduces prefill energy and EC by up to 16.8% and 28.7%, respectively; for edge autonomous vehicle perception, it achieves 12.0% energy and 23.6% EC reductions under real-time latency constraints.

sources.title: System-performance and cost modeling of Large Language Model training and inference
sources.abstract: Large language models (LLMs), based on transformer architectures, have revolutionized numerous domains within artificial intelligence, science, and engineering due to their exceptional scalability and adaptability. However, the exponential growth in LLM size and complexity has outpaced advancements in compute capacity, memory bandwidth, network performance, and cost efficiency, posing significant challenges to their scalability on distributed systems. To address these limitations, alternative model architectures, optimization strategies, communication-aware network topologies, and novel system design approaches have been proposed in literature. This paper introduces a performance-cost modeling methodology for LLM training and inference that integrates state-of-the-art compute techniques with memory optimizations, and latest communication techniques. Building on an analytical performance model, our approach incorporates recent innovations such as the flash attention technique and mixture of experts models to address the memory bandwidth and compute bottlenecks. It also considers the impact of different network topologies and topology-specific communication algorithms with 5D parallellism. The framework also integrates a chiplet cost model. The proposed modeling methodology provides valuable insights to guide future compute system design and facilitates hardware-software co-development, in particular due to its ability to analyze performance-cost trade-offs for various system architectural configurations.

sources.title: Recent Advances and Trends in Chiplet Design and Heterogeneous Integration Packaging
sources.abstract: Abstract In this study, chiplet design and heterogeneous integration packaging, especially (a) chip partition and heterogeneous integration driven by cost and technology optimization, Figs. 1(a) and 1(b) chip split and heterogeneous integration driven by cost and yield, Figs. 1(b) and 1(c) multiple system and heterogeneous integration with thin-film layers directly on top of a build-up package substrate, Figs. 1(c) and 1(d) multiple system and heterogeneous integration with an organic interposer on top of a build-up package substrate, Figs. 1(d) and 1(e) multiple system and heterogeneous integration with through-silicon via (TSV) interposer on top of a build-up package substrate, Fig. 1(e), will be investigated. Figures 1(c)–1(e) are driven by formfactor and performance. Emphasis is placed on their advantages and disadvantages, design, materials, process, and examples. Some recommendations will also be provided.

sources.title: ChipletPart: Cost-Aware Partitioning for 2.5D Systems
sources.abstract: Industry adoption of chiplets has been growing as chiplets are a cost-effective option for making large, high-performance systems. Consequently, partitioning large systems into chiplets is increasingly important. In this work, we introduce ChipletPart, a cost-driven 2.5D system partitioner that addresses the constraints of chiplet systems, including complex objective functions, limited reach of inter-chiplet I/O transceivers, and the assignment of heterogeneous manufacturing technologies to different chiplets. ChipletPart integrates a sophisticated chiplet cost model with a genetic algorithm (GA)-based technology assignment and partitioning methodology, along with a simulated annealing (SA)-based chiplet floorplanner. Our results show that ChipletPart: (i) reduces chiplet cost by up to 58% (20% geometric mean) compared to state-of-the-art min-cut partitioners, which often yield floorplan-infeasible solutions; (ii) generates partitions with up to 47% (6% geometric mean) lower cost compared to the prior work Floorplet; (iii) reduces chiplet cost up to 48% (30% geometric mean) compared to Chipletizer, while consistently producing I/O-feasible chiplet solutions across all testcases; and (iv) for the testcases we study, heterogeneous integration reduces cost by up to 43% (15% geometric mean) compared to homogeneous implementations. Additionally, we explore Bayesian optimization (BO) for finding low cost and floorplan-feasible chiplet solutions with technology assignments. On some testcases, our BO framework achieves better system cost (up to 5.3% improvement) with higher runtime overhead (up to 4x) compared to our GA-based framework. We also present case studies that show how changes in packaging and inter-chiplet signaling technologies can affect partitioning solutions. Finally, ChipletPart, the underlying cost model, and our testcase generator are available as open-source tools.

sources.title: FoldedHexaTorus: An Inter-Chiplet Interconnect Topology for Chiplet-based Systems using Organic and Glass Substrates
sources.abstract: Chiplet-based systems are rapidly gaining traction in the market. Two packaging options for such systems are the established organic substrates and the emerging glass substrates. These substrates are used to implement the inter-chiplet interconnect (ICI), which is crucial for overall system performance. To guide the development of ICIs, we introduce three design principles for ICI network topologies on organic and glass substrates. Based on our design principles, we propose the novel FoldedHexaTorus network topology. Our evaluation shows that the FoldedHexaTorus achieves significantly higher throughput than state-of-the-art topologies while maintaining low latency.

sources.title: Emerging Chiplet-Based Architectures for Heterogeneous Integration
sources.venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology
sources.abstract: This article explores the semiconductor industry's pivotal shift from traditional monolithic system-on-chip designs to chiplet-based architectures employing heterogeneous integration. As Moore's Law scaling encounters fundamental physical and economic barriers at advanced nodes, chiplet approaches offer a compelling alternative by disaggregating complex systems into smaller functional blocks manufactured separately and then integrated using advanced packaging technologies. This paradigm delivers substantial advantages in manufacturing yield, cost efficiency, development time, and performance optimization while enabling specialized acceleration for emerging workloads. The article explores how leading companies have implemented chiplet strategies, examines the critical role of advanced packaging technologies as enabling infrastructure, identifies key technical challenges requiring industry-wide solutions, and discusses how this architectural evolution is reshaping intellectual property models and business relationships throughout the semiconductor ecosystem. By exploring emerging research directions in three-dimensional integration, photonic interconnects, heterogeneous materials integration, and AI-optimized design tools, this work provides a comprehensive perspective on how chiplet-based architectures are fundamentally transforming semiconductor system design and manufacturing.

sources.title: Photonic-Interconnected Quantum Chiplets for Modular and Networked Quantum Computing
sources.venue: International Journal of Academic and Industrial Research Innovations(IJAIRI)
sources.abstract: Abstract: This study investigates photonic-interconnected quantum chiplets as a modular hardware pathway for scalable and networked quantum computing. The central problem is that monolithic quantum processors face compounding constraints in yield, wiring density, cryogenic routing, interconnect loss, calibration complexity and non-local connectivity. Photonic interconnection offers a technically plausible route to divide a large quantum computer into smaller processors while preserving quantum communication across modules through fibre links, photonic switches, optical transduction or integrated photonic interposers. The paper develops an academically rigorous framework that connects quantum-chiplet architecture, photonic integration, quantum error correction, control latency and manufacturability. It uses secondary real-data anchors from recent public demonstrations and a transparent engineering analysis to evaluate whether modular photonic networking can satisfy requirements for distributed logical qubits, entanglement generation and fault-tolerant operation. Results indicate that photonic chiplets can reduce scaling penalties relative to a monolithic wiring strategy when interconnect loss, feed-forward latency and module yield are jointly optimized. The study concludes that photonic-interconnected chiplets are not a minor packaging improvement but a possible architectural transition comparable to the movement from single-die classical processors to heterogeneous chiplet systems. The strongest contribution is a system-level evaluation model that links physical photonic performance with computer-architecture metrics and identifies the practical thresholds that must be met for Nature-level experimental validation. Keywords quantum computing chips, photonic chiplets, modular quantum computing, quantum interconnects, distributed quantum processors, silicon photonics, quantum networking, fault-tolerant quantum computing, optical interposers, quantum error correction, entanglement routing, wafer-scale quantum manufacturing, cryogenic control, quantum architecture, quantum hardware scalability

sources.title: Evaluating Vulnerability of Chiplet-Based Systems to Contactless Probing Techniques
sources.abstract: Driven by a need for ever-increasing chip performance, a growing number of semiconductor companies are opting for all-inclusive System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures. Increasingly, the solution adopted to minimize the impact of silicon defects on manufacturing yield of larger dies has been to split a design into multiple smaller dies called chiplets, which are then brought together on a silicon interposer. Advanced 2.5D and 3D packaging techniques that enable this kind of integration also promise increased power efficiency and opportunities for heterogeneous integration.However, despite their advantages, chiplets are not without issues. Disaggregating a design into multiple separate dies introduces new security threats, including the possibility of tampering with and probing exposed data lines. In this paper we evaluate the exposure of chiplets to probing by applying laser contactless probing techniques to a chiplet-based AMD/Xilinx VU9P FPGA. First, we identify and map interposer wire drivers, and show that probing them is easier compared to probing internal nodes. Lastly, we demonstrate that delay-based sensors, which can be used to protect against physical probes, are insufficient to protect against laser probing.

sources.title: Delegato: Locality-Aware Atomic Memory Operations on Chiplets

sources.title: A Comparative Study of Monolithic and Chiplet CPU Architectures: Performance and Yield Perspectives
sources.venue: IIAE International Conference on Industrial Application Engineering (ICIAE)
sources.abstract: In this study, we implement two versions of a dual-core CPU—one monolithic and one chiplet-based—and conduct comparative evaluations from the perspectives of performance and manufacturability. First, both architectures are designed under identical conditions using a RISC-V (RV32I) single-cycle core and a write-through cache, and their performance is measured through simulations using Vivado. The results show that under test programs with simple instruction sequence, the chiplet architecture achieves higher execution performance than the monolithic architecture under certain clock settings. For manufacturability, we estimate die area based on LUT utilization and apply the Poisson yield model to compute the number of functional dies per 300-mm wafer. While both architectures exhibit decreased yield with increasing defect density, the chiplet architecture—constructed from smaller dies—shows a more gradual decline, resulting in up to approximately a 10% difference in the number of functional products. These findings indicate that chiplet architectures offer clear advantages in manufacturability and can also provide performance benefits under specific access patterns.

sources.title: FAPlace: Joint Optimization of Chiplet Placement and Interposer Footprint for 2.5D Systems
sources.venue: ACM Great Lakes Symposium on VLSI (GLSVLSI)
sources.abstract: The placement of chiplets on a silicon interposer is a pivotal step in 2.5D system integration, yet existing placement approaches typically assume a pre-defined interposer footprint. This creates a circular dependency: the optimal footprint cannot be known without first solving the placement, while the placement itself is constrained by the given dimensions. An undersized interposer may exclude feasible placements, while an oversized one yields unnecessarily sparse solutions. Moreover, even when the footprint area is minimized, few existing approaches explicitly control the interposer’s aspect ratio. To jointly address these challenges, we propose FAPlace, a footprint aware mask guided sequential placement framework. FAPlace operates on a sufficiently large canvas, eliminating the circular dependency by allowing the optimal interposer footprint to emerge as an output of the optimization rather than a pre-specified input. At its core is a novel footprint mask that fuses area compactness with an aspect ratio penalty into a unified spatial cost map. Integrated with wirelength and thermal guidance masks, FAPlace delivers holistic multi-physics optimization in a deterministic, single pass process. Experimental results demonstrate that FAPlace reduces wirelength and footprint area while achieving near-unity aspect ratios, without compromising on thermal performance.

sources.title: CarbonPATH: Carbon-aware pathfinding and architecture optimization for chiplet-based AI systems
sources.abstract: The exponential growth of AI has created unprecedented demand for computational resources, pushing chip designs to the limit while simultaneously escalating the environmental footprint of computing. As the industry transitions toward heterogeneous integration (HI) to address the yield and cost challenges of monolithic scaling, minimizing the carbon cost of these complex HI systems becomes critical. To fully exploit HI, a co-design approach spanning application, architecture, chip, and packaging is essential. However, this creates a vast design space with competing objectives, specifically the trade-offs between performance, cost, and carbon footprint (CFP) for sustainability. CarbonPATH is an early-stage pathfinding framework designed to address this multi-objective challenge. It identifies optimized HI systems by co-designing workload mapping, architectural parameters, and packaging technologies, while treating sustainability as a first-class design constraint. The framework accounts for a wide range of factors, including compute and memory sizes, chiplet technology nodes, communication protocols, integration style (2D, 2.5D, 3D), operational CFP, embodied CFP, and interconnect type. Using simulated annealing, CarbonPATH explores this high-dimensional space to identify solutions that balance traditional metrics against environmental impact. By capturing interactions across applications, architectures, chiplets, and packaging, CarbonPATH uncovers system-level solutions that traditional methods often miss due to restrictive assumptions or limited scope.

findings.claim: Splitting a design into chiplets creates new physical-security exposure. Interposer wire drivers can be mapped and probed with laser contactless techniques, and delay-based protective sensors were shown to be insufficient against laser probing.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: This is one conference paper that tests a single commercial device, a chiplet-based VU9P FPGA. It shows a real attack surface but does not show how general the exposure is across other chiplet products or what mitigations cost. Whether the exposure is exploitable in deployed systems is a gap.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Disaggregating a design into multiple separate dies introduces new security threats, including the possibility of tampering with and probing exposed data lines.

findings.claim: Chiplets add non-uniform memory-access latency relative to monolithic dies. This degrades synchronization primitives such as atomic memory operations and needs new microarchitectural workarounds, so the performance case for chiplets is workload-dependent.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: The abstract states the penalty directly and proposes a mitigation (Delegato). The paper is a MICRO architecture study, so the harm is likely simulation-based. Its magnitude on commercial parts is not in the abstract.
findings.supporting_excerpt: chiplets impose higher and non-uniform memory access (NUMA) latencies than monolithic integration.

findings.claim: Many headline chiplet benefits rest on analytical models, simulation or small testcases rather than fabricated silicon. Examples are the 1.52x throughput, 0.27x energy and 0.89x cost versus monolithic in Chiplet-Gym, and the cost reductions in ChipletPart. Real-world transfer is unproven in these abstracts.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: Chiplet-Gym says it 'analytically model[s]' PPAC. ChipletPart reports gains only 'for the testcases we study', and its geometric-mean gains (6% to 30% versus prior tools, 15% for heterogeneous versus homogeneous) are far below the maxima quoted. CarbonPATH calls itself 'early-stage'. ChipletPart and CarbonPATH are arXiv preprints and not peer reviewed. The results are model outputs that depend on the cost-model assumptions, and the abstracts give no silicon validation.

findings.claim: The yield advantage of chiplets is shown with a toy comparison, and the study's own numbers are modest. A dual-core RV32I design on an FPGA toolflow with a Poisson yield model gave up to about a 10% difference in functional dies. The paper's phrase 'clear advantages' therefore overreaches for realistic large SoCs.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The design is tiny. Die area is estimated from LUT utilization, performance comes from Vivado simulation on simple instruction sequences, and the chiplet performance gain appears 'under certain clock settings'. The abstract does not include packaging, known-good-die test or assembly yield loss, which is the usual counterweight to die-yield gains. Those omissions are a gap and not evidence of failure.

findings.claim: Chiplets do not remove the memory-bandwidth, network and cost bottlenecks of large AI systems. A modeling paper states that LLM growth has outpaced compute, memory bandwidth, network performance and cost efficiency, and it treats chiplet cost as one input to system trade-offs.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: This is an arXiv preprint with a truncated abstract, so it does not say how much chiplets help or hurt these bottlenecks. It is context showing that disaggregation addresses die yield and cost but not necessarily the other limits.
findings.supporting_excerpt: the exponential growth in LLM size and complexity has outpaced advancements in compute capacity, memory bandwidth, network performance, and cost efficiency

findings.claim: Packaging and inter-chiplet interconnect choices remain unsettled and add integration risk. Options span organic substrates, organic or TSV interposers, thin-film layers and emerging glass substrates. Each has its own advantages and disadvantages, and new topologies are still being proposed for them.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The packaging review lists several integration routes and says it will examine their 'advantages and disadvantages'. FoldedHexaTorus (an arXiv preprint) treats glass substrates as 'emerging', and FAPlace shows interposer footprint and placement still being optimized. Together these suggest no converged packaging or interconnect solution. The abstracts give no manufacturing-maturity, cost or reliability data for glass, so the timing is only suggestive.

findings.claim: Photonic-interconnected quantum chiplets are presented as a possible architectural transition, but the evidence is a conceptual engineering analysis using secondary data. The benefit is conditional on jointly optimizing interconnect loss, feed-forward latency and module yield, which the abstract does not show being achieved.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The paper appears in a low-visibility journal and relies on 'secondary real-data anchors' and 'transparent engineering analysis' rather than new experiments. Its own problem statement lists yield, cryogenic routing, interconnect loss and calibration complexity as compounding constraints. The long horizon is my judgement and is not stated in the abstract.

findings.claim: Sustainability and thermal costs of heterogeneous integration are not yet well quantified in these sources. Carbon-aware design is described as early-stage, and the placement work reports only that thermal performance is not compromised, with no numbers in the abstract.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: CarbonPATH (an arXiv preprint) treats embodied and operational carbon as a design constraint but the abstract is cut off before any result. FAPlace asserts thermal parity without quantification. This is a gap in the evidence, not proof of a problem. Stacked and multi-die thermal limits remain a plausible risk that the abstracts do not test.

hype_flags: 'Fundamentally transforming semiconductor system design' (src_5414723b87): promotional framing from a low-visibility venue, and the abstract does not quantify its claimed advantages.

'Not a minor packaging improvement but a possible architectural transition' for quantum chiplets (src_641a33128a): based on a conceptual analysis with secondary data, and conditional on several unsolved optimization targets.
'Clear advantages in manufacturability' (src_e66f051609): drawn from a toy dual-core design, simulation and a model-based yield estimate of roughly 10%.
'Chiplets are a cost-effective option' (src_eec1d1a032): cost gains come from the authors' own cost model and selected testcases, and the average gains are much smaller than the maxima.
The 'game changer' framing of chiplets (src_20f2377341): the same paper documents higher NUMA latency that harms atomic operations.

finding.claim: S1 overstates its evidence. The 'largely manual' claim comes from a single 2023 position paper. The abstracts do not call design automation 'the main obstacle'; they say it is needed to realise the benefits, or that it is an active research focus. The survey describes automation as a 'popular focus', which suggests the field is moving beyond fully manual design. Labelling this 'verified_fact' with high confidence is too strong.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: Only one cited abstract makes the manual-process statement, and it is from 2023. The survey says 'Currently, optimizing the automation methodologies for chiplet architecture is a popular focus', and Floorplet says only that floorplanning has 'received limited attention'. 'Main obstacle' is the Science agent's inference, not a quoted finding, and the high confidence is not justified.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Despite progress made in various related domains, the design of chiplets remains largely reliant on manual processes.

finding.claim: S2 treats the cost and yield benefit as an established finding, but the cited abstracts only assert it as background motivation. The only quantitative evidence available is weak: a toy FPGA/Poisson comparison with about a 10% difference in functional dies, and model-based cost numbers. The cost and yield advantage of 3D stacking is not shown at all. Describing this as 'verified_fact' conflates an author claim with a demonstrated result.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: This MFIT sentence is introductory framing with no data behind it in the abstract. The one abstract that tests yield (src_e66f051609) reports only 'up to approximately a 10% difference' on a dual-core RV32I design. The Chiplet-Gym cost advantage comes from an analytical model. So 'motivated by' is supportable, but 'verified' relative to monolithic ICs is not.
finding.supporting_excerpt: These approaches offer a significant cost reduction and higher manufacturing yield than monolithic 2D integrated circuits.

finding.claim: S3 says thermal management is 'repeatedly flagged as the key physical limiter', but only MFIT states a thermal challenge explicitly. The placement-order paper uses temperature as one optimisation metric and reports only a 1.01% peak-temperature improvement. That figure undercuts the idea that thermal is the dominant limiter and does not show thermal is being 'attacked'. The micro-fluidic cooling claim rests on one automotive review preprint with simulation-only evaluation.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The cited abstracts do not rank thermal against other limiters such as interconnect latency, NUMA effects or packaging. 'Key' is an unsupported ranking. The thermal gain in the placement paper is marginal compared with its wirelength gain.
finding.supporting_excerpt: applying the top-ranked placement order obtained from the learning to rank network results in a 10.05% reduction in total inter-chiplet wirelength and a 1.01% improvement in peak system temperature

finding.claim: S4 repeats the MFIT authors' claim of 'negligible accuracy loss' without noting that the abstract gives no accuracy figure, no reference simulator and no validation against measured hardware. It is a single arXiv preprint with no citation record. The 'days to seconds' speedup is also not a like-for-like comparison against a named baseline.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: 'Negligible' is an author characterisation with no error bound in the abstract. The claim is based on one non-peer-reviewed source, and the abstract does not show whether the models were checked against silicon or only against other simulators.
finding.supporting_excerpt: these models can reduce execution times from days to mere seconds and milliseconds with negligible loss in accuracy.

finding.claim: S5 claims a shift 'from hand-tuned heuristics to learned optimisers', but the cited and available papers do not show learned methods displacing classical ones. Chiplet-Gym explicitly combines RL with non-RL optimisers 'to ensure robustness'. ChipletPart reaches its cost gains with a genetic algorithm and simulated annealing, and FAPlace uses a deterministic single pass. The placement-order paper only refines an existing RL placer, with small gains. Three or four papers do not establish a trend.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The Chiplet-Gym quote shows that RL alone was not relied upon. ChipletPart uses GA and SA, and FAPlace is a deterministic single-pass framework, both from other abstracts. The 'shift' is the Science agent's extrapolation, and RL is not shown to beat non-learned baselines.
finding.supporting_excerpt: We also explore non-RL-based optimization approaches and combine these two approaches to ensure the robustness of the optimizer.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S6 says the hexagonal arrangement was 'measured' to beat a grid in latency and throughput. The abstract says only 'in practice' and does not say whether this is hardware measurement or simulation. Chiplet counts of tens to hundreds are very unlikely to have been fabricated. A single conference paper also does not show that geometry is treated as a 'first-class design variable'. FoldedHexaTorus shows interconnect topology is still being actively revised.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstract does not state the evaluation method, so 'measured' is an unsupported upgrade, and simulation is the likelier reading. FoldedHexaTorus proposes a new topology claiming 'significantly higher throughput than state-of-the-art topologies', which implies HexaMesh is not settled as the preferred arrangement.
finding.supporting_excerpt: in practice (latency reduced by 19%; throughput improved by 34%)

finding.claim: S9 presents large efficiency reductions (48.5% to 97.8%) for Fengshui as a verified result. They come from one arXiv preprint, with a baseline of 'homogeneous accelerators', and the reported figures are from the authors' own framework and models. The cost metrics (EC, EDPC) depend on assumed NRE and cost models that the abstract does not detail. The preprint's listed date (2026-09-10) is also unusual, which suggests metadata issues.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: These are author-reported results from a co-design framework, not independent or silicon-measured ones, and the comparison baseline is chosen by the authors. The abstract is truncated in the evidence, so the exact baselines are not visible. The 'verified_fact' label should mean 'reported by the authors', not 'demonstrated'.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Fengshui-generated BASICs achieve 48.5%, 88.1%, 93.0%, and 97.8% reductions in energy, energy-cost product (EC), energy-delay product (EDP), and energy-delay-cost product (EDPC)

finding.claim: S10 attaches a market statistic to chiplets that does not support the 'lead application domain' claim. The 20-22 billion figure is a forecast for automotive compute chips in general, not for chiplets. It is stated without a source in a review preprint whose own evidence is gem5 simulation and design studies. Supply-chain resilience is asserted, not shown.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The quote shows the number describes demand for automotive compute chips overall, not chiplet adoption. Nothing in the abstract shows automotive is leading chiplet adoption, or that a design has been qualified for automotive use. It is a single preprint, and automotive-grade reliability is not addressed.
finding.supporting_excerpt: surging demand for automotive compute chips, expected to reach 20-22 billion by 2030.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S11 says the dependence on open interoperability and shared composition standards is a 'recurring framing across the abstracts'. The 'circular dependency' wording appears only in Fengshui, and Fengshui does not mention standards. The Automated Design of Chiplets abstract mentions neither interoperability nor standards. Only the automotive review mentions an 'open Chiplet ecosystem'. Two of the three cited papers do not support the claim, which is the Science agent's own synthesis.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The circular dependency is about choosing a chiplet pool and designing accelerators, not about interoperability standards. 'Shared composition standards' does not appear in any cited abstract. The finding links a design-methodology problem to a standards argument that the sources do not make.
finding.supporting_excerpt: choosing which chiplets to build and how to compose them into accelerators is circularly dependent

finding.claim: The findings omit the performance and security downsides of disaggregation. S1 to S12 present chiplets as cost-effective and promising, with thermal and EDA as the main open issues. Several available abstracts show other costs: packaging adds latency, memory access becomes non-uniform and hurts synchronisation, and exposed interposer wires create probing exposure that delay-based sensors do not stop. The performance benefit is therefore workload-dependent and the integration risk is understated.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: Floorplet itself says 'additional latency introduced by advanced packaging can decrease performance', and the probing paper says disaggregation 'introduces new security threats'. Neither downside appears in the Science findings, even though S8 touches on reliability.
finding.supporting_excerpt: chiplets impose higher and non-uniform memory access (NUMA) latencies than monolithic integration.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

limitations: Only titles and abstracts were available, and several abstracts are truncated, so results, caveats and methods in the full papers are unseen.

The set has 12 papers, skewed toward EDA and design-space optimization, with little on manufacturing yield data, known-good-die test, UCIe or other standards, supply-chain concentration, or advanced-packaging capacity constraints.
Several sources are arXiv preprints or low-citation papers (0 to 6 citations), and some come from low-visibility venues, so they are not reliable evidence.
No paper compares chiplets against alternatives such as wafer-scale integration or monolithic designs on newer nodes, so displacement risk could not be assessed.
Absence of data on thermal, reliability, cost and supplier dependence in these abstracts is a coverage gap, not evidence that those problems exist.
Only titles, metadata and abstracts were available, and several abstracts are truncated, so I could not check methods, baselines or whether results come from simulation or hardware.
I did not challenge S7, S8 or S12. They are modest and match their abstracts, though S12's 'converging' rests on only three papers.
The evidence set is small (23 papers) and weighted towards arXiv preprints and EDA or placement work. Contradicting industry or silicon data may exist but was not retrieved.
Some metadata (for example the 2026-09-10 date on Fengshui) looks anomalous. I flagged it but could not verify it.
I did not assess whether specific numbers (for example 1.52x throughput) are reproducible or what baselines they use.

sources.title: ELECTRIC-FIELD SHUNT FOR HYBRID BONDING INTERFACES [US20260354205A1]
sources.abstract: Advancements in semiconductor packaging technology have faced challenges such as signal integrity loss, parasitic capacitance, and limited interconnect density in stacked chip configurations. These challenges are addressed by introducing hybrid bonding interfaces (HBIs) and a novel grounding mechanism for through-silicon vias (TSVs). HBIs enable fine-pitch, high-density interconnects through direct metal-to-metal or dielectric-to-dielectric bonding, eliminating the need for microbumps. TSV grounding reduces the metal-insulator-semiconductor (MIS) effect by shunting electric fields to ground metal layers and ground HBIs. This grounding mechanism improves broadband return loss and insertion loss performance, mitigating parasitic effects. These advancements enhance electrical performance, reduce capacitive coupling effects, and improve signal integrity in high-speed data transfer applications.

sources.title: HYBRID BONDING TECHNIQUES THAT UTILIZE MULTI-FUNCTIONAL BARRIER MATERIALS [US20260344498A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Semiconductor devices with dual-function barrier layers for hybrid bonding are disclosed herein. A semiconductor device can include a first substrate having a first dielectric layer and first bond pads disposed thereon, a second substrate having a second dielectric layer and second bond pads disposed thereon, and a barrier layer disposed between portions of corresponding first and second bond pads. The first substrate can be hybrid bonded to the second substrate via the dielectric layers and bond pads. The barrier layer can be configured to inhibit diffusion and/or migration of conductive material from the first bond pad into the second dielectric layer and/or from the second bond pad into the first dielectric layer. The barrier layer can comprise platinum group metals, two-dimensional materials, or graphene-modified copper materials, and can promote diffusion between corresponding bond pads while inhibiting diffusion into dielectric layers.

sources.title: CERTIFIED TELEMETRY DATA COLLECTION IN CHIPLET PROCESSOR ARCHITECTURE [US20260339808A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Aspects of establishing certified telemetry in processing circuitry, including in a chiplet-based implementation, are described. An example method performed by telemetry monitoring circuitry includes: obtaining telemetry data produced from compute operations performed in one or more hardware resources (e.g., compute tiles, memory controllers, etc.) of a compute platform; generating a signature of the telemetry data, based on a hash or derivation of the telemetry data; and communicating certified telemetry data to an external entity, to provide the telemetry data and the signature of the telemetry data. In further examples, the certified telemetry data is collected, validated, and aggregated from multiple chiplets of a package or system-on-chip, to provide a certification of telemetry data collected across multiple hardware elements. The certified telemetry data may be used for purposes such as performance monitoring, service level agreement (SLA) compliance, resource usage tracking, security event analysis, and the like.

sources.abstract: A transaction layer protocol for communicating HBM traffic over die-to-die physical layer interfaces (and associated systems, devices, and methods) is disclosed herein. In one embodiment, a memory system includes a processing unit, a high bandwidth memory (HBM) device including a base die, and a die-to-die interface communicatively coupling the processing unit and the base die. The processing unit and the base die each include a HBM access protocol (HAP) adapter configured to implement an HBM access protocol for communicating HBM traffic over the die-to-die interface. The HBM access protocol can define packet structures optimized for HBM traffic and methods for packing and unpacking HBM traffic within die-to-die interface packets. The die-to-die interface can be a Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) interface.

sources.title: GLOBAL RAS DECISION AND DVFS ALLOCATOR WITH PER DIE MONITORS AND CONTROLLERS IN CHIPLET ARCHITECTURES [US20260329452A1]
sources.abstract: A method and system for managing dynamic voltage/frequency scaling (DVFS) and aging in chiplet-based system on integrated circuit (SoIC) architectures are disclosed. The method involves resetting multiple dies upon power-up, each equipped with local DVFS controllers and monitors to measure operating parameters such as voltage, temperature, and workload indicators. A global DVFS allocator receives performance data from the local monitors, adjusts DVFS credit allocations based on a calibrated global DVFS policy, and communicates power shifting instructions to the local controllers. Aging uniformity is managed by a global reliability, availability, and serviceability (RAS) controller, which retrieves historical aging data from retention memory and applies adjustments to optimize system reliability. The system includes a global DVFS allocator, a global RAS controller, and retention memory for storing operational parameters and aging data. This approach enhances performance, reliability, and resource allocation in semiconductor technologies, particularly for SoIC architectures.

sources.abstract: [0000]    A system for monitoring optical computing components is disclosed. The system may include processors and non-transitory computer-readable media comprising instructions. The system may receive optical measurements from optical interconnects internal to a distributed computing system, where the optical interconnects couple distributed computing components each having an associated optical communication device enabling optical communication at a package level. The system may receive performance metrics of the distributed computing components comprising workload activity, synchronization behavior, or thermal conditions. The system may input the optical measurements and performance metrics into an artificial intelligence model trained to predict potential faults. The system may determine a fault domain comprising a chiplet interface, an optical engine, a laser source, a coupler, or a reconfigurable optical path. The system may generate a message comprising a repair recommendation, an alert, or an automated corrective action based on the fault domain.

The second instructions may be generated by determining a flow of processing sub-operations for the operation in question and allocating resources to each. This may be done by a pre-trained model. A performance characteristic may be provided for each sub-operation for optimisation. In an embodiment the instructions correspond to different instruction set architectures. In an embodiment the first instructions may comprise prefixes that determine an algorithm for generating the second instructions and a body for generating the second instructions. The algorithm may depend on a state of the interface unit. The algorithm may be a vector processing algorithm. The interface unit may comprise a non-integrated element seperate from the processor cores that may be arranged in a chip or chiplet separate to the chip or chiplet of the processor cores. The interface unit may comprise an element integrated within an integrated processor core, which may be arranged in a chip or chiplet with the integrated processor core. Figure 2

sources.title: CHIP STACK STRUCTURE, MANUFACTURING METHOD THEREFOR, CHIP PACKAGE STRUCTURE, AND ELECTRONIC DEVICE [WO2026200137A1]
sources.abstract: Embodiments of the present application relate to the technical field of electronics, and provide a chip stack structure, a manufacturing method therefor, a chip package structure, and an electronic device, for use in improving hybrid bonding quality and improving yield of the chip stack structure. In the chip stack structure, between a first chip and a second chip, in addition to a sixth dielectric layer for filling a gap, a fourth dielectric layer and a fifth dielectric layer are further comprised. The fourth dielectric layer covers a side surface of a first circuit layer in the first chip, and the fifth dielectric layer covers a side surface of a second circuit layer in the second chip. The fourth dielectric layer and the fifth dielectric layer can cover molten slag debris on the side surfaces of the circuit layers, preventing the molten slag debris from scattering, and improving cleanliness of a bonding surface between a first bonding layer and a third bonding layer and a bonding surface between a second bonding layer and the third bonding layer, thereby improving the bonding effect of hybrid bonding and improving product yield.

sources.title: METHODS OF FORMING BRIDGE CHIPLET SHIELD STRUCTURES [EP4815713A2]
sources.abstract: [0001]    Microelectronic integrated circuit package structures include a substrate comprising an IC die on a surface of the substrate, where a first edge of a bridge die is below a portion of the IC die and is embedded within the substrate. The bridge die is coupled to the IC die, and a dummy die is adjacent to the IC die on the substrate, where a second edge of the bridge die is below the dummy die.

sources.title: MEMORY CHIPLET ARCHITECTURE AND SEMICONDUCTOR PACKAGE STRUCTURE USING THE SAME [US20260300190A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Disclosed is a memory chiplet architecture including one or more memory banks. Each memory bank includes an arbiter and a memory, and the memory is addressed. The arbiter of each memory bank is configured to perform arbitration according to an incoming access command and an address space of the memory bank where it resides, to determine to access data of the memory, transmit control signals, and/or forward the incoming access command. Therefore, the number of memory banks can be adjusted according to different storage capacity requirements. Besides, the memory bank that communicates with the outside of the memory chiplet architecture is provided with an input/output interface, so that it communicates with an external chip to increase storage capacity and/or bandwidth. In addition, a memory chiplet using the memory chiplet architecture can be applied to a 3D semiconductor package structure or a 2.5D semiconductor package structure.

draft.summary: Research on chiplets is growing quickly: OpenAlex works rose from 495 to 743 in 2024-2025 (+50.1%), and the 2026 year-to-date count is up 53.9%. These counts are not adjusted for overall growth in publishing. Company filings show chiplet integration and advanced packaging already being offered commercially by Intel, AMD, Marvell and equipment suppliers [M1][M2][M3][M4][M5], and patent filings centre on hybrid bonding, die-to-die protocols and system management [P1][P2][P3]. Much of the academic evidence for cost and yield benefits rests on simulation, models or toy comparisons rather than silicon [R3][R4][C2], and Risk challenges weaken several Science claims, including the 'design automation is the main obstacle', 'learned optimisers are displacing heuristics' and 'open standards are a recurring framing' claims [C1][C5][C9]. Performance, security and packaging-choice risks are real [R1][R2][R6], and Marvell itself flags chiplet advances as a possible source of obsolescence [M10]. The three chiplet-linked large-cap stocks are down sharply with very high volatility [T7]. The main uncertainty is whether chiplet economics hold up at scale across workloads, and which suppliers capture the value.
draft.plain_summary: Chiplets are small chips that are combined into one package instead of building a single large chip. Research, patents and company reports all show they are being taken up, especially for AI. The main thing that could slow this is that many claimed benefits are still only proven in simulations, and that packaging, heat and security problems are not settled.

Process complexity and metrology demand are rising [M9]. Patents focus on hybrid bonding yield [P1]. The listed stocks are down sharply with very high volatility [T5][T7]. Filings describe positioning, not confirmed order volumes.

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: Demand for hybrid bonding and die-on-wafer integration could grow with AI-driven 3D IC scaling [M4], but packaging options (organic, interposer, glass) remain unsettled [R6]. Kulicke & Soffa itself warns that alternative packaging could shift volume away from its wire-bond products [M6]. Winners are therefore not yet clear.

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: The evidence says little directly about this horizon. Intel frames the industry as moving from monolithic to chiplet-based architectures [M1], which is a company view, not a demonstrated outcome. Thermal and reliability limits could constrain dense stacks [S3][S8][C3].

bull.label: forecast

base.label: forecast

bear.label: forecast
